_help: Add actions for Benefit Management (benefits) and Benefit Realisation (benefit_realisation), offline, then load this file with 'Add actions from a JSON file' on the Assessment page.
Put each NEW action as a row in the 'actions' list (copy the examples). Only component, lens and action are required.
component: benefits or benefit_realisation. lens: Planning and Risk, or Process and Sustainment.
action: the text. Start with 'M ' (must) or 'S ' (should) to set the priority.
status: Planned, In Progress, Blocked, Completed, Cancelled or Skipped (default Planned). owner: a name. startDate / dueDate: yyyy-mm-dd. All optional.
Existing actions are never changed, and an action already in that lens is skipped.

'existing' lists what the app already has for each pathway, for reference only so you do not repeat it. It is ignored on import. Benefit Realisation has no Not Started to Embedding actions yet, so that is the best place to add.

benefits.action: S Recognise the importance of benefits realisation as part of successful change delivery.
S Begin discussions with sponsors and leaders about the expected value of the change.
M Engage key stakeholders to explore potential organisational and stakeholder benefits.
M Capture initial ideas regarding expected benefits and possible disbenefits.
M Identify stakeholder groups likely to experience benefits from the change.
M Gain initial leadership support for benefits identification and management activities.
S Review available evidence that may indicate potential benefits.
S Begin raising awareness that benefits will need to be defined, measured and realised.
S Facilitate structured benefits workshops with sponsors, leaders and subject matter experts.
M Document and categorise expected organisational, operational, financial and user benefits.
M Document likely disbenefits and trade-offs associated with the change.
M Develop measurable benefit statements and draft success criteria for priority benefits.
M Identify proposed benefit owners and establish accountability for benefit realisation.
M Develop stakeholder-specific ‘What’s in it for me?’ (WIIFM) benefit statements.
S Validate with stakeholders which benefits are most important and meaningful to them.
S Review and validate draft benefits with stakeholders and sponsors.
S Assess differences in expected value across stakeholder groups and business areas.
S Refine benefit definitions, ownership and measures using stakeholder feedback.
M Obtain approval and baseline the benefits realisation approach.
M Define measures, KPIs and reporting arrangements for each benefit and record this in the benefits register.
M Establish baseline measures against which benefits can be assessed and include in the business case.
M Develop a benefits realisation plan including ownership, timelines and reporting.
M Integrate benefits tracking into governance and programme reporting.
M Use stakeholder-facing benefit messages (WIIFM benefits) to build support and momentum.
S Communicate expected benefits and success measures to stakeholders.
S Gather stakeholder feedback on benefit assumptions and expectations.
S Validate that benefit measures are meaningful and understood by stakeholders.
S Monitor stakeholder confidence in the expected benefits.

benefit_realisation.action: M Track benefit performance against agreed KPI's, measures and targets.
S Review realised, unrealised and unexpected benefits through governance forums.
M Identify risks to benefits realisation and agree mitigation actions.
M Assess whether expected benefits are being achieved and if not, why.
S Manage dependencies that affect benefit realisation (RAID log).
S Share evidence of realised benefits and unintentional consequences with stakeholders.
S Use stakeholder insight to understand barriers to achieving benefits.
S Monitor stakeholder perceptions of realised benefits and improvement.
M Use WIIFM benefit stories and examples to reinforce adoption.
S Recognise teams and individuals contributing to benefit realisation.
M Continuously monitor long-term benefit realisation.
S Embed benefits management into normal business and adoption management processes.
S Refine benefit measures and approaches using organisational learning.
S Use benefit evidence to inform future investment and change decisions.
S Maintain management of long-term dependencies affecting realised benefits.
M Promote a culture of continuous benefits realisation and adoption.
S Regularly communicate realised benefits and improvement outcomes.
S Use stakeholder feedback to identify opportunities for further benefits realisation.
S Measure ongoing stakeholder perception of benefit delivered by the change.
S Use success stories and achievements to sustain belief in the value of the change.

S Confirm the process and behaviour changes required to realise each benefit.

S Agree benefit owners and baselines before each service starts rollout.
S Track benefits from the start of each rollout wave.
S Check that required process changes are being applied in practice.
S Provide support where adoption is not translating into expected benefits.
S Review the pilot benefits plan, assumptions, dependencies and risks.
S Identify benefits requiring new baselines or owners for wider rollout.
S Confirm balancing measures to detect displaced workload or unintended effects.
S Update the benefits plan for each rollout wave and service.
S Assign owners, measures, baselines, dependencies and review dates.
S Agree how benefits evidence will inform rollout and investment decisions.
S Collect benefit data and report progress through governance.
S Manage dependencies and risks that could delay or reduce benefits.
S Escalate gaps in data quality, ownership or delivery action.

benefit_realisation.action: S Compare benefit performance across services, roles and rollout waves.
S Investigate where benefits are lower or different from expectations.
S Share effective practices that have improved benefit realisation.
S Embed benefits monitoring within routine operational performance management.

S Review measures regularly to ensure sustained value is still being captured.
S Review benefits against targets and approved assumptions.
S Agree recovery actions where benefits are off track.
S Use evidence to adjust sequencing, support or future rollout scope.
S Transfer benefit ownership and reporting into business as usual.
S Anticipate and manage risks to sustained benefits.
S Use long-term benefit trends to guide optimisation and future investment.
